display.purpose: Page titles. The home headline scales to its column; a painting's title is one step smaller.

headline.purpose: Section headings, reduced slightly inside the band and beside the hero painting.

title.purpose: A painting's title under its card and the heads of small groups.

body.purpose: All running text, capped at 68ch. Prices and navigation use weight 500.

label.purpose: Medium and size lines, notes, captions, field errors, footer.

pigment-note.purpose: Penciled pigment names under swatches, and nothing else.

shadows.name: painting-rest
shadows.purpose: Every painting image lying on the panel.

shadows.name: painting-lifted
shadows.purpose: A card's painting on hover, with a 3px rise.

shadows.name: button-hover
shadows.purpose: Primary buttons on hover, with a 1px rise.

shadows.name: swatch-edge
shadows.purpose: Keeps pale pigments visible on the ground. Not elevation.

shadows.name: shadow-tint-light
shadows.purpose: RGB triplet behind every shadow in the light scheme.

shadows.name: shadow-tint-dark
shadows.purpose: RGB triplet behind every shadow in the dark scheme.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for every animation and transition.

motion.name: brush-swatch
motion.value: clip-path wipe left to right, .55s, delay calc(var(--i) * 90ms + 120ms)
motion.purpose: Loading the palette: swatches brush in one after another when rendered.

motion.name: brush-chips
motion.value: clip-path wipe left to right, .45s, delay calc(var(--i) * 50ms)
motion.purpose: Card chips brush in again on card hover or focus.

motion.name: button-press
motion.purpose: Primary button rise of 1px on hover and sink of 1px when pressed.

motion.name: card-lift
motion.purpose: A card's painting rises 3px on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none; transition: none; scroll-behavior: auto
motion.purpose: Applied to everything under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

narrative.overview:
The site is a gessoed panel with a paint box open beside it. The ground is a cool white, the writing is ivory black, and the interface owns no accent of its own. All color on a page comes from the painting in view: its five pigments are laid down next to it as rough brushed swatches, each with its name penciled underneath in a pen script, and the darkest of the five inks the buttons and the home page band. Move to another painting and the page is mixed again from that painting's tubes.

Everything that is not paint stays quiet and square. One grotesque handles all type, from the headline to the price. Corners are sharp, rules are a pencil line, and the only things with depth are the paintings themselves, which lie on the panel with a soft shadow beneath them, and the one button that sells them. Density is low: a painting, its swatches, what it costs, one button.

The world was chosen over the white portfolio grid, where color belongs only to the images. Here the paint leaves the picture and reaches the page.
keyCharacteristics: Cool gesso ground, ivory black ink, no fixed accent
Five pigment swatches travel with every painting, as large brushed patches on feature views and as a thin chip strip on cards
The darkest pigment of the painting in view is written to `--deep` and colors primary buttons, the band, the caret and the text selection
One type family for everything; a pen script reserved for pigment names
Square corners on all interface elements; only the swatches have a rough brushed edge
Swatches brush in from left to right, one after another
Light and dark schemes follow the visitor's system setting

rules.name: The Borrowed Color Rule
rules.body: The stylesheet holds neutrals, one error red and one fallback green. Every other color on screen is a pigment from `data/works.js`, and it appears only as a fill: a swatch, a chip, a button, the band. Pigments are never used as text color on the ground.

rules.name: The Deepest Pigment Rule
rules.body: `--deep` is the pigment with the lowest luminance among the five, and it is accepted only when white text on it reaches a contrast of 4.5 to 1. If no pigment qualifies, Spruce stays. Never set `--deep` by hand to a color that fails this test.

rules.name: The Ink For State Rule
rules.body: Selected, pressed, focused and checked states are drawn in the text color (Ivory Black in light, its counterpart in dark), not in pigment. Pigment marks the way to a purchase; ink marks where you are.

rules.name: The One Hand Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque sets every word of interface and content. Hierarchy comes from size and from three weights (400, 500, 600, with 700 for the wordmark alone), never from a second family, capitals, or wide tracking.

rules.name: The Pencil Rule
rules.body: Nanum Pen Script writes pigment names under swatches. It is never used for headings, prices, buttons, quotes or decoration.

rules.name: The Only Paintings Lift Rule
rules.body: A soft shadow means "this is an object": a painting or the button that buys one. Text blocks, the band, inputs, filters and the footer stay flat on the ground.

rules.name: The Paint Is The Only Rough Edge Rule
rules.body: If it is interface, its corners are square and its edges straight. If it is a swatch of paint large enough to hold the filter (2.5rem or taller), its edge is brushed. Nothing is rounded.

dos: Do show a painting's five pigments wherever the painting appears: brushed swatches with penciled names on feature views, the chip strip on cards.
Do let `script.js` set `--deep` from the painting in view, and use `--deep` with white text for primary buttons and the band.
Do keep every interface corner at 0 radius and every rule at 1px.
Do show paintings whole, at their true proportion, with the painting shadow beneath them.
Do write button labels that name the item and the price.
Do draw selected, pressed and focused states in the text color.
Do define both schemes for any new neutral, and check a new pigment set on the dark ground as well as the light one.
Do keep entrance motion to the brush wipe, and honor `prefers-reduced-motion`, which turns all animation and transitions off.
donts: Don't add a fixed brand accent to the stylesheet. Spruce is a fallback for pages with no painting, not a brand color to spread.
Don't use pigment colors as text on the ground, or tint the ground itself with them.
Don't set Nanum Pen Script on anything except pigment names.
Don't round corners, and don't apply the brush filter to anything that is not a swatch of paint.
Don't crop paintings to a uniform ratio, or put badges, ribbons or overlays on the image.
Don't give cards, text blocks or sections a panel background or a shadow. Only paintings and the primary button lift.
Don't add scroll reveals, parallax or fades. Apart from the brush wipe, movement is limited to a rise of 1 to 3px on hover.
Don't use Alizarin for anything but form errors.
